 Dated 03.06.2016 Of Ld. Adm,

J U D G M E N T :
Fsat No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16
Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. Fso Page 2 of 16
 1.0

Vide this common judgment, I shall dispose of all 
the above three appeals against the same order dated 03.0
6.2016  ("the impugned order" in short) passed by
the Ld. Adjudicating  Officer/Addl. District Magistrate (North East) ("ADM" in short),

directing the appellants Food Business Operator Sh. Sarfuddin, (in  FAST No. 44/16), Supplier Sh. Bhumesh Kumar (in FAST No. 
43/16) and Manufacturer Sh. Karan Jain (in FAST No. 45/16) to  pay a penalty of Rs.20,000/, Rs. 30,000/ and Rs.50,000/, 
respectively, under Sections 52 & 58 read with section 49 of the  Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 ("FSS Act" in short) for  violation of sections 26(1) & 26(2)(ii) read with sections 3(1)(a) & 
3(1)(zf)(a) FSS Act and Regulations 2.2.2.10 & 2.3.1.5 of Food  Safety & Standards (Packaging & Labeling) Regulations, 2011  ("FSS (P&L) Regulations" in short), within 7 days from the date of  order.
1.1
Appellant Karan Jain (FSAT No. 45/2016) is the  proprietor of Suppliercummanufacturing firm M/s.
Nanaji
Bakers & Confectioners, 40/7, Street No.1, Samay Pur Industrial
Area, Delhi110042

. Appellant Bhumesh Kumar (FSAT No. 
43/2016) is the proprietor of the Supplier firm M/s Ganpati Trading  FSAT No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. FSO Page 3 of 16  Company, 25/87, Gali No.14, Vishwas Nagar, Shahdara, Delhi 110032 and the appellant Sarfuddin (FSAT No. 44/2016) is the  proprietor of FBO firm namely M/s Aameer Breakfast Corner, E 166/9, Gali No.17, Shastri Park, Delhi110053.

2.0 Facts in brief which are not in dispute are, that:
 (i) on 7th July, 2015, Food Safety Officer ("FSO" in   short), purchased 8 sealed packets of "Zeera Cookies", 
Vide This Common Judgment vs The State Of Bihar & Another on 28 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55494564/
2  from the possession of appellant Sarfuddin, Proprietor   of M/s Aameer Breakfast Corner (FBO firm), where   the said food article was found stored for sale for human   consumption.
One counterpart of the sample under   sealed cover was sent to Food Analyst on 08.07.2015.

The Food Analyst vide his report dated 22.07.2015   opined the sample as misbranded because of   violation of Regulation 2.2.2.10 of FSS (P&L) 
 Regulations.

He also found the sample to be misleading   as it was violative of Regulation 2.3.1.5 FSS (P&L) 
 Regulations.

The Food Analyst also reported that Best   before was declared in small letters on outer label as   "Best before upto 6 months from the date of packing. 
FSAT No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V.
FSO Page 4 of 16
Further, nutritional value declared on outer and inner  labels
are different, which is misleading.

But   none of the appellants preferred appeal against the Food   Analyst's Report; 
 (iii) appellant Sarfuddin, Proprietor of FBO M/s   Aameer Breakfast Corner, at the time of taking sample   was looking after the business of the said firm on day to   day basis.
Notices of the same were issued to all the appellants and   hearing was given.
The appellants admitted aforesaid   violations and prayed for leniency.

After considering   the matter, Ld. ADM observed that despite proper   opportunity, all the appellants failed to establish tha  "Zeera Cookies" manufactured by appellant Karan Jain   of M/s Nanaji Bakers & Confectioners were not   misbranded and misleading and found that they were   liable to a penalty as envisaged under Sections 52 & 58   of the FSA, Rules & Regulations framed thereunder.

He   accordingly vide order dated 03.06.2016 imposed   penalty on the appellants as under:
 i) Rs.20,000/ (Rupees Twenty Thousand only) upon  FSAT No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. FSO Page 6 of 16  appellant Sh. Sarfuddin, Proprietor of FBO; 
 ii) Rs.30,000/ (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) 
 upon appellant Sh. Bhumesh Kumar,
 Proprietor,Supplier Firm M/sGanpati Trading Company;
 iii) Rs.50,000/ (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) upon  Sh. Karan Jain, Proprietor of Supplier Firm cum   Manufacturing Firm.
3.0

All the appellants have challenged the above order of  Ld. ADM dated 03.06.2016 pleading that the impugned order was  passed without considering the facts and the evidence on record and  without appreciating the law as applicable.

3.1 The appellant Bhumesh Kumar/supplier (FAST No. 
43/2016) has submitted that he is an FBO and had purchased the  sample commodity from the manufacturer Karan Jain, Proprietor of  M/s Nanaji Bakers and Confectioners; and that it is the admitted  case of the complainant/FSO that the sample commodity was in  sealed condition as purchased from the manufacturer (M/s Nanaji  Bakers & Confectioners). Hence, he could not have been held liable.
FSAT No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. FSO Page 7 of 16

3.1.1 Appellant Sarfuddin (FAST No. 44/2016) has also  taken a similar plea that the Ld. ADM failed to appreciate that the  sample commodity was purchased by him from the  supplier/appellant Bhumesh Kumar and was sold in sealed  condition.

sentences.text: 3.1.2 Both the above appellants have also pleaded that they  cannot be held responsible for printing and declaration on the label  of the said commodity.

3.1.3 The appellant Karan Jain/manufacturer (FAST No. 
45/2016)
has contended that there has been substantial compliance  of the regulations 2.2.2.10 of FSS (P&L) Regulations as the required  information was printed on the label.
No prejudice has been caused  to the consumer of the product.
Thus, the prosecution launched  against the appellants was unwarranted.

It is submitted that the  information (best before) had been printed in small letters therefore, 
the appellant cannot be held guilty of misbranding u/S 2(ix)(k) of  the PFA Act and placed reliance upon the judgment of Hon'ble  Patna High Court in M.D. Anand Aqua, M/s S.B. Industries, 
FSAT No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. FSO Page 8 of 16  Patna Vs. The State of Bihar & another, 2011(1) FAC 265, and  that of Hon'ble Jharkhand High Court in Md. Shree Om Industries  Vs. State of Jharkhand and another, 2012 (2) FAC 8, Oscar  Joseph & another Vs. The State of Jharkhand and another ,2012  FAC 74 and Sri Jalaj Kumar Chatterjee Vs. State of Jharkhand  and others, 2013 (1) FAC 482.

sentences.text: It is also pleaded that Regulation  2.3.1.5 does not apply to biscuits.
It is further submitted that even  otherwise, the report of Food Analyst, is vague.

Food Analyst has  failed to disclose the name of test which was carried out by him, 
while detecting the colour in the sample commodity.

The Food  Analyst has not disclosed what were the nutritional information  declared on the label and which nutritional information(s), were  different in the outer & inner label of the sample commodity.
3.2 All the appellants have also challenged the impugned  order on the ground that they were given to understand by Ld. ADM  that as per complete investigation, the case is made out against them  for which penalty has to be imposed.

In view of which they had no  option but to move an application for pleading guilty before the Ld. 
ADM on 23.02.2016.

The appellants Bhumesh Kumar and  Sarfuddin have pleaded that they were under the impression that  they were not liable, being neither the manufacturer nor the packer  FSAT No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V. FSO Page 9 of 16  of the sample commodity.
Appellants Bhumesh and Karan Jain have

also pleaded that at the time of compounding, the appellants were  asked to furnish certain documents/information including ITR, 
which was furnished.

Thereafter, the Ld. ADM imposed heavy fine  without appreciating that the appellants Sarfuddin and Bhumesh  were neither the manufacturer nor the packer of the commodity, 
thus, had not committed any offence.

On the other hand, Ld. Addl.PP for the State submitted  that this appeal is not maintainable as the appellants voluntarily  pleaded guilty before the Ld. Trial Court.
They cannot now raise the  contentions as raised by them in their appeals.
Even otherwise, they  have no case on merits.
Further, having pleading guilty, they cannot  even challenge the fine imposed upon them vide impugned order.
5.0 I have heard Sh. Kapil Sharma, Advocate for all the appellants and Sh. A.K. Mishra and Sh. Anil, Ld. Addl. PP for the  State and have perused the record carefully.
6.0 Admittedly, the sample of Zeera Cookies was lifted  from M/s Aameer Breakfast Corner, E166/9, Gali No.17, Shastri  Park, Delhi - 110053 (FSAT No. 44/2016) on 07.07.2015.
Food  FSAT No 43/16, 44/16 & 45/16 Bhumesh Kumar, Sarfuddin & Karan Jain V.
FSO Page 10 of 16  Analyst

vide his report dated 22.07.2015 reported the sample to be  "misbranded" in view of violation of Regulation 2.2.2.10 of FSS  (P&L) Regulation and also found it to be "misleading" because of  violation of Regulation 2.3.1.5 of FSS (P&L).

The relevant portion  of report of The Food Analyst dated 22.07.2015, reads as under :

But Section 375  (b) Cr.PC permits the accused who has pleaded guilty to challenge the conviction "to the extent  or legality of the sentence."
The present appeal is thus maintainable only to that extent.

The appellants have contended that as the label  m e n t i o n e d b e s t b e f o r e d a t e t h o u g h n o t i n c a p i t a l l e t t e r s , i t w a s a  s u f f i c i e n t c o m p l i a n c e , i n v i e w o f t h e a f o r e s a i d j u d g m e n t s i n M . D .

Thus, the packet of sample  commodity/cookies was required to comply with the said Regulation.

It has come on  record that although the outer label declared presence of synthetic food colour (127) 
i n t h e s a m p l e F S A T N o 4 3 / 1 6 , 4 4 / 1 6 & 4 5 / 1 6 c o m m o d i t y b u t t h e s a m e w a s a c t u a l l y n o t f o u n d o n a n a l y s i s . T h e  a p p e l l a n t s c a n n o t n o w b e a l l o w e d t o t a k e t h e p l e a t h a t t h e s a m e d o e s  not in any manner affect the nutritional value of the commodity, having pleaded guilty.

9.0 However, considering the above facts, particularly that the label did mention Best Before  D a t e ,

All the three appeals are  partly allowed, accordingly.
